instruction: I need my parents to have a venmo account. Last time I checked none had one. Make an account for whoever that does not have it yet, using their email address and A}2Gm4r as password. Then send them a phone text message, "I have created a venmo account for you. Please activate it, you should have received an email for it. I've set your password to be A}2Gm4r. Change it soon too.".
notes: Parents are discovered via phone.search_contacts(relationship="parents"); their emails/names/phone numbers are runtime-bound placeholder objects tied to parent-1/parent-2 by static contact-* facts. Whether a parent already has a Venmo account is unknown at planning time, so (consistent with 'last time I checked none had one' and the closed-world init) the plan checks each parent with venmo.search_users(query=email), signs up each parent lacking an account with the given password, and texts each parent whose account was created. At runtime, if venmo.search_users shows a parent already has an account, the agent treats (has-venmo-account p) as true and skips signup and the text for that parent (the 9-call reference corresponds to exactly one parent lacking an account). parent-1/parent-2 are domain constants so supervisor-complete-task can carry the ground goal conditions with no parameters. Phone login username is the supervisor's phone number; venmo username is the supervisor's email. venmo.signup needs no token; it sends a verification email, which accounts for the gmail changes in the evaluation. No answer is needed for complete_task.
